data.body:
## 2609 failed the API-surface gate -- and that is the THIRD gate make lint does not cover

The narrowed monitor's first firing was a genuine defect in MY OWN change. 2609 (S6) fails on three
ubuntu pytest cells with:
  FAILED tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py::test_committed_baseline_matches_live_surface
  AssertionError: Public API surface drift detected against the committed baseline
S6 adds GateCongestedError, GateScratchUnavailableError and the gate_admission module without
regenerating the committed baseline. Base already carries the 9a17 fix, so this is not the e2e flake
-- it is 2609's own.

Sent back with the SANCTIONED path, which differs from the mechanism-delta baseline in an important
way: scripts/gen_api_surface.py:35 documents 'python scripts/gen_api_surface.py --update  # rewrite
the baseline after an intended change'. So THIS baseline is contributor-regenerable, whereas the
mechanism one is explicitly not. Worth keeping straight -- treating them the same would either block
a legitimate change or invite a forbidden hand-edit. Also asked the agent to review every added line
before committing the regeneration: a baseline refresh is exactly where an unintended export slips in
and silently becomes a compatibility obligation.

FILED 1035-bed7-c855-4732 / refreshing-gauche-guineafowl (p2) for the pattern rather than leaving a
fourth agent to rediscover it. THREE gates are pytest-only and invisible to make lint:
  test_mechanism_delta.py            -> caught change 2601 at Gerrit; make lint was exit 0
  test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py -> caught change 2600 at Gerrit
  test_api_surface_gate.py           -> caught change 2609 at Gerrit; make lint was exit 0
In every case the author had run make lint AND make typecheck and seen them pass.

The framing that matters: make lint is the DOCUMENTED contract -- AGENTS.md names it, the pre-commit
hook runs it, and every agent brief treats it as the local proxy for CI. A proxy that returns green
for a tree CI will reject is worse than no proxy, because it converts 'I verified locally' into a
false statement made in good faith. Three agents made exactly that statement tonight, all correctly
following instructions.

Deliberately did NOT propose moving everything into make lint -- the full pytest tier would be far
too slow for a commit gate, which is presumably why these live where they do. The defect is the
CONTRACT, not the placement, so the ticket offers three resolutions and names documentation-only as
the weakest but honest option. Also folded in the related git-add skew: the parity gate considers only
tracked paths, so running it before 'git add' gives a green that flips red once the file is staged.

Linked relates_to 90c7 and a1f1, both of which are instances of the same underlying problem: a gate
whose local behaviour differs from its CI behaviour.
